paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: everything you give to God started out in His hands. David gives a mountain of gold, the leaders pile on more, and then David prays, "But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? For everything comes from You, and from Your own hand we have given to You." (1 Chronicles 29:14) So the people weren't showing off, they were handing back what God had handed them. That takes the pressure off, baker, because you can't out-give the One who gave you the oven, the flour AND the kitchen.

Now look at HOW they gave. The text says they "had given to the LORD freely and wholeheartedly" (1 Chronicles 29:9), and David says God tests the heart (1 Chronicles 29:17). I think that's the part God cares about most. A gift with a grumble on it is like a batch I stamped while sulking, and a gift with joy in it is a batch I'm NOT dignified about. David even asks God to keep that desire in his people's hearts, so a willing heart is something we can ask God for too (1 Chronicles 29:18).

And then the handoff. David knows Solomon is young and inexperienced, so he doesn't just leave him a to-do list. He prays that God would give Solomon "a whole heart" to keep His commandments and build the temple (1 Chronicles 29:19). David's long reign ends, Solomon takes the throne, and the work goes on because God's purposes were never riding on one man. So give what you have with a glad heart, pray for the ones coming after you, and trust that the LORD finishes what He starts.
